title: Last Remaining Hong Kong Protest Sites to Be Cleared
main_content:
Hong Kong police have warned protesters they have until Thursday to clear the territory’s remaining protest sites, in what may bring to an end more than two months of pro-democracy demonstrations.

Police spokesman Cheung Tak-keung urged the demonstrators to start removing obstacles at the protest sites and leave peacefully so the roads can be reopened.

He said police will not tolerate any violence and will take action against “radicals and troublemakers.”

Police are set to move in after a ruling by Hong Kong’s High Court gave authorities permission to tear down street barricades, tents and other obstructions from the protesters’ main camp in the Admiralty district near government headquarters.

The injunction was published Tuesday in local media, which reported that thousands of police will work Thursday with bailiffs to clear the tent city. The order only gives permission to dismantle a portion of the Admiralty site, but authorities are expected to clear the entire area and reopen traffic.

The South China Morning Post reports police will also break up a separate, smaller protest site in the popular shopping district of Causeway Bay.

The move sets the stage for a possible final showdown between police and protesters, who have repeatedly clashed during past attempts to clear the sites.

Only dozens now remain at the protest sites. At one point, tens of thousands participated, calling for fully democratic elections for the city’s top leader in 2017.

questions.question: What has the police warned the protesters to do?
options: To escalate their demonstrations in solidarity with each other
To clear the protest sites peacefully by Thursday
To relocate to a designated assembly area outside the city
To gather more supporters to strengthen their cause
questions.answer: To clear the protest sites peacefully by Thursday

questions.question: What did the Hong Kong’s High Court rule?
options: To allow the continuation of protests indefinitely
To give police permission to tear down part of the protest site in Admiralty
To ban police from intervening in the protests
To provide protection to protesters against police action
questions.answer: To give police permission to tear down part of the protest site in Admiralty

questions.question: What could happen after this injunction will be put in place?
options: A potential increase in public support for the protesters
A confrontation leading to violent clashes between police and protesters
The organization of a new series of protests throughout Hong Kong
A temporary halt in all civic activities in the area
questions.answer: A confrontation leading to violent clashes between police and protesters
